propositions: A nested `rebar bridge` CLI group must expose only functional `preview` (read-only, dry-run forced) and `sync` (mutating, live forced) verbs with no placeholder extensions.
The `bridge` group must reject `--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and arbitrary trailing arguments to preserve the read/write contract distinction.
Preview must perform zero Jira writes and zero ticket or bridge-state writes; sync must perform persisted mutations while preserving unrelated event state.

Unknown nested verbs must fail with valid choices and never dispatch a same-named top-level command; help text must omit internal vocabulary (`mode`, `rank`, `gate`, `lock`, `cap`, `pass`, `binding store`, numeric exit codes).
Legacy top-level spellings (`reconcile`, `jira-onboard`, `bridge-probe`, `bridge-fsck`, `doctor`) remain unchanged; `Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, and `gated_mode: reconcile-check` remain intact.

Documentation (`cli-reference.md`, `exit-codes.md`, `user-guide.md`, `release-notes.md`) must describe only the staged surface that ships; the nested group is provably generated by `gen_cli_reference.py`.
